what_it_does: Cameras embedded in small devices like drones or smart doorbells capture far more raw pixel data than the weak onboard processor can compress and transmit efficiently, creating a major energy bottleneck. Standard compression schemes (like JPEG) are designed for human viewing, not for feeding a machine-learning vision model, so they waste bandwidth on image details the AI does not need. SNAPPIX takes a different approach called coded exposure (CE): instead of capturing a full frame and then compressing it, the camera's sensor shutter opens and closes in a learned pattern during a single exposure, blending only the most informative light samples into the final pixel values right inside the sensor before any data moves anywhere. The sampling patterns are learned from data using ideas from efficient coding theory (the mathematical principle that a good code spends bits where information is densest). A companion vision model is designed alongside the sensor so it can handle the non-uniform pixel values that result, and only minor hardware additions to the existing sensor circuitry are needed to support the new capture mode.
